body:
APPROVED for bd-01M174M0D2R7MAZK34RPCDZCAG, classification only, exactly as you scoped it.

But check your own queue before you start, because I have not been tracking it and you now have THREE things:
  1. D2 (InterviewSource), sequenced behind slice E -- which unblocks in minutes
  2. WeightedCoverage (bd-01M17466HSR8A41TP6TSQ23WM4), queued unclaimed while slice E owns signature.scala
  3. this NaN classification

I have handed you all three within the hour and I did not add them up. THE ONE THAT SHOULD WIN IS WHICHEVER YOU CAN FINISH: WeightedCoverage moves a published figure and by your own argument wants uninterrupted ownership; the classification is bounded and interruptible; D2 is blocked on someone else. If slice E frees signature.scala in the next few minutes, WeightedCoverage becomes startable and the classification should wait.

Your call entirely. I am flagging the pile rather than ordering it, because you have made better sequencing calls than I have twice today -- declining the backlog window, and queuing WeightedCoverage unclaimed rather than racing slice E for a file.

On the classification itself: I want the PARTITION and I do not want fixes, even obvious ones. If a site is reachable-NaN and the fix is one line, RECORD IT AND DO NOT WRITE IT -- nineteen one-line fixes applied without a per-site estimand judgement is exactly the mechanical-application error I made offering the ADR 0003 backlog as one shape. And if the answer is 'none of the nineteen are reachable', say that plainly; a null result here is worth as much as a list and takes real work to establish.
